title: Add a task to a Kanban board
description: Add a task to a chosen lane on an Obsidian Kanban board by capturing after the lane heading, with optional date formatting
requires: a board with at least one lane
afterImport: In **Settings → QuickAdd**, click the cog next to **Add task to board** and set **Capture to** to your board file. Until you do, QuickAdd asks which file to capture to on every run.
Cards go to the top of the `## Backlog` lane. If your lane has another name, change **Insert after** to match its heading, for example `## To do`.
Run **Add task to board** from the command palette and type your task.

title: Add an inbox item
description: Create a timestamped inbox note from a template, naming the file with the current date and time plus your input
afterImport: Run **Inbox item** from the command palette and type a short name. QuickAdd creates and opens a timestamped note in `Inbox/`.

Optional: to use another folder, click the cog next to **Inbox item** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, remove `Inbox` from the list under **New note location**, type your folder in **Folder path**, and click **Add**.

title: Add entries to your daily note
description: Cookbook of Capture recipes that add timestamped lines, tasks, quotes, callouts, and table rows to today's daily note
requires: the **Daily notes** core plugin, or Periodic Notes 0.0.17, managing your daily notes (Periodic Notes 1.0 beta isn't supported)
afterImport: Each capture writes to [`{{DAILY}}`](/docs/FormatSyntax/#daily), the note **Open today's daily note** opens. A missing note is created from your daily notes template.
Run any of the five from the command palette, or run **QuickAdd: Run**, choose **Daily note**, and pick one. The heading or callout it writes under is created when missing.

title: Add location long-lat from address
description: Macro and user script that geocode an address into a location latitude-longitude property on the active note, for the Map View plugin
requires: an internet connection (addresses are looked up on OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service; no account needed)
afterImport: Open the note you want to place, run **Add location from address** from the command palette, and enter an address. A specific address (street, city, country) gives the best match.
The note's `location` property becomes `lat,lng`, replacing any earlier value. Map View is optional: install it if you want to see the note on a map.

title: Book finder script
description: Insert book details fetched from the Google Books API into your vault using a Macro choice and template, no API key required
requires: an internet connection (titles are looked up on Google Books; no API key needed)
afterImport: Notes land in `Books/`. To use another folder, click the cog next to **Add book note** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, then the cog on the **Book note** step, and change **Folder path**.
Run **Add book note** from the command palette and enter a book title (a short clipboard text is prefilled). The first Google Books match becomes the note; there is no picker.
If Google Books answers with a quota error, try again later. It does not mean the book was not found.

title: Brain dump
description: Jot down several inbox entries in a row - a macro opens a Capture again after each entry until you press Esc
afterImport: Run **Brain dump** from the command palette, or give it a hotkey in **Settings → Hotkeys**.
Optional: to put entries somewhere other than `Inbox.md`, hover over **Brain dump entry** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, click its cog, and change **Capture to**.
Optional: to repeat a Capture you already have, hover over **Brain dump** and click its cog, then click the cog on the **brainDump** step and enter that Capture's name in **Capture choice**.

title: Canvas capture
description: Capture formatted text into a selected Canvas card or a specific node in a .canvas file, with supported write positions and linking
afterImport: Open a canvas and select exactly one text card or Markdown-file card. Run **Add idea to card** from the command palette and type your idea. It is added as a bullet at the bottom of the card.

Optional: to always write to the same card, click the cog next to **Add idea to card** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, turn off **Capture to active file**, set **Capture to** to your `.canvas` file, and pick the card under **Target canvas node**.

title: Capture to inbox with GPS
description: Append a timestamped inbox line with device GPS coordinates, for offline capture on Obsidian mobile 1.11+
requires: Obsidian mobile 1.11 or newer for GPS (desktop saves the line without coordinates)
afterImport: Optional: in **Settings → QuickAdd**, click the cog next to **Capture to Inbox with GPS**, then the cog on the **captureInboxGps** step, to change **Inbox path** (default `Inbox.md`).
Run **Capture to Inbox with GPS** from the command palette, or give it a hotkey. On mobile, allow location access when asked.

title: Change properties in your daily notes
description: Update a property in your daily note by picking it from a suggester and entering a new value, using Obsidian's frontmatter API
requires: either the **Daily notes** core plugin turned on or a custom **Daily note path** on its script step
afterImport: Create today's daily note and give it the properties you want to change; the menu only lists properties that already exist, and only text, number and checkbox ones.
Run **Change daily note property** from the command palette, pick a property, and enter its new value.

Daily notes somewhere else? Click the cog next to **Change daily note property** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, then the cog on the **changeDailyProperty** step, and set **Daily note path** (for example `bins/daily/{{DATE:YYYY-MM-DD - ddd MMM D}}.md`). Leave it empty to use the Daily notes plugin's folder and date format.

title: Create a meeting note and start typing
description: Create a meeting note or add a project update, then keep typing where you put the CURSOR marker.
afterImport: Run **New meeting** from the command palette and answer the prompt. The note lands in `Meetings/`; change **Folder path** on the choice to use another folder.
Open any project note in **Live Preview**, click in the note body, and run **Add project update** to append a dated section and start typing under **Progress**.

title: Create an MOC note with a link dashboard
description: Create a map-of-content note with an embedded Base dashboard showing its backlinks and outgoing links, via a Template choice
requires: the Bases core plugin, enabled in **Settings → Core plugins**
afterImport: Run **New MOC note** from the command palette and enter a title. The note lands in `MOCs/`; change **Folder path** on the choice to use another folder.

title: Fetch tasks from Todoist
description: Import Todoist tasks into a note using a macro and user script, selecting from all tasks, a project, or a single section
requires: a Todoist API token, copied from **Settings → Integrations → Developer** in Todoist
afterImport: In **Settings → QuickAdd**, click the cog next to **Todoist**, then the cog on the **todoistTaskSync** step. Paste your token into **Todoist API token** and click the save icon next to the field. QuickAdd keeps it in Obsidian's secret storage, not in `data.json`.
**Imported tasks are completed in Todoist by default**, and recurring tasks move to their next occurrence. Untick **Complete imported tasks in Todoist** in the same settings to leave them open.

Run **Import Todoist tasks** from the command palette and pick which tasks to fetch: all of them, one project, or one section. They are written to `Todoist tasks.md`; change **Capture to** on the choice to use another note.

title: Insert a related notes Base into an MOC note
description: Insert a live Base view of related notes into an active MOC note by capturing from a .base template into the current file
afterImport: `MOC Related Notes.base` lands in your QuickAdd template folder if you set one, otherwise in `Templates/`. You can change that path under **Files** while importing.
Open your MOC note, run **Insert related notes base** from the command palette, and type a line of context.

title: Log book to daily journal
description: Log the book you are reading to your daily journal note's Book property with an input prompt and Obsidian's frontmatter API
requires: either the **Daily notes** core plugin turned on or a custom **Daily note path** on its script step
afterImport: Create today's daily note if you have not yet; the macro does not create one.
Run **Log book** from the command palette and enter a title. It sets the `Book` property of today's note, replacing any earlier value.

Daily notes somewhere else, or another property? Click the cog next to **Log book** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, then the cog on the **logBook** step, and set **Daily note path** (for example `bins/daily/{{DATE:YYYY-MM-DD - ddd MMM D}}.md`) or **Property name**. Leave the path empty to use the Daily notes plugin's folder and date format.

title: Migrate Dataview properties to frontmatter
description: Migrate inline Dataview properties to YAML frontmatter with wikilink-aware comma handling and selective property lists
afterImport: Try it on a copy of a note first: migrated inline fields are removed from the note body.

In **Settings → QuickAdd**, click the cog next to **Migrate Dataview properties**, then the cog on the **migrateDataviewToFrontmatter** step. Set **Properties to Migrate** to the fields you want moved (default `Reference, Related`); turn on **Migrate All Properties** only if you want every inline field moved.
Open the note you want to migrate and run **Migrate Dataview properties** from the command palette. Only that note changes.

title: Move notes with a tag to a folder
description: Move every note carrying a chosen tag to a target folder, matching both frontmatter and inline tags, via a macro script
afterImport: Back up your vault first. Picking the destination folder moves every matching note at once, with no preview or undo; to reverse it, move the notes back.

Run **Move notes with a tag** from the command palette, pick a tag, and choose whether nested tags count too (`#project/work` when you picked `#project`). The folder menu shows how many notes will move.
Notes whose path contains `template` (in any case, such as `Templates/`) are left where they are.

title: Movie & series script
description: Insert a movie or TV show note from the OMDb API into your vault with a Macro choice and template, requires an API key
afterImport: In **Settings → QuickAdd**, click the cog next to **Add movie note**, then the cog on the **movies** step. Paste your key into **OMDb API Key** and click the save icon next to the field. QuickAdd keeps it in Obsidian's secret storage, not in `data.json`.

Run **Add movie note** from the command palette and search for a title or IMDb id (like `tt0111161`). The note lands in `Movies/`; change **Folder path** on the **Movie note** step to use another folder.

title: My book notes template
description: Pull a book's highlights from Readwise into a new note using a Template choice and a bundled highlight-fetching macro
requires: a Readwise account and its [access token](https://readwise.io/access_token)
afterImport: In **Settings → QuickAdd**, click the cog next to **Readwise**, then the cog on the **readwise** step. Paste your token into **Readwise access token** and click the save icon next to the field. QuickAdd keeps it in Obsidian's secret storage, not in `data.json`.

Run **Add Book Notes** from the command palette and pick a book. The note is named after it and lands in `Books/`, with the book's highlights under **Highlights & Notes**; change **Folder path** on the choice to use another folder.

title: Toggl manager
description: Start preset Toggl Track time entries from a customizable menu using a macro and the Obsidian Toggl integration plugin
afterImport: If you have not already, install and enable **Toggl Track integration** from **Settings → Community plugins → Browse**. In its settings, paste the token from the bottom of your [Toggl profile](https://track.toggl.com/profile) into **API Token**, click **connect** to check it, then pick your workspace under **Toggl Workspace** (click its refresh icon if the list is empty). The token lives in the Toggl plugin, not in QuickAdd.

Open `scripts/togglManager.js` (or wherever you put it during import) in a text editor and edit the `menu` object: each sub-menu has a `togglProjectName`, which must match a project in that workspace exactly, and `menuOptions`, where the left side is the label you see and the right side is the description Toggl gets. Save the file.
Run **Toggl manager** from the command palette, pick a project, then an entry to start the timer.

title: Zettelizer
description: Create a linked note from each heading of a chosen level in your active file, naming it after the heading text
afterImport: By default each `###` heading gets a note in `Zettels/` (created if missing) that embeds that section; the source note is not changed. The file name is the heading minus its first word, so one-word headings are skipped, and so are names that already exist.

To change the folder or heading level, click the cog next to **Zettelize headings** in **Settings → QuickAdd**, then the cog on the **zettelizer** step: **Folder for new notes** (empty means the vault root) and **Heading level**.
Open the note you want to split up and run **Zettelize headings** from the command palette.
